headline: High risk: OpenHands can write/browse/egress by default while caveman uses MCP and shared files, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman uses MCP and reads/writes project files like CLAUDE.md, while OpenHands can use MCP, browse, and process files in its runtime. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if OpenHands content is surfaced into caveman’s trusted file or MCP inputs. The exact bridge is not documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF OpenHands output is copied into caveman-managed files or MCP messages
IF caveman treats file or MCP content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP on one side for the shared workflow
Route OpenHands output through a human review step before caveman ingests it
Restrict caveman to read-only access to shared instruction files
Add provenance tags to any OpenHands-generated text
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents into separate workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while OpenHands reads files mounted into its runtime and has broad network egress. If those files contain sensitive data, OpenHands can transmit them outward by default. The pairwise path is inferred from documented file access plus egress, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF sensitive data is placed in files mounted into OpenHands
IF OpenHands is allowed to send runtime context to external model providers
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the mounted runtime
Use a local-only model provider for OpenHands
Redact secrets from project notes before sharing
Mount a minimal read-only workspace
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data classification filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and uses MCP, while OpenHands can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run subprocesses inside a shared mounted volume. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state. The overlap is directly supported by both profiles, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or mounted volume
IF OpenHands and caveman can write overlapping files or git refs
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize git operations through one operator
Make caveman read-only on shared repos
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces content-writing outputs and OpenHands can act on files, shell, and git. If OpenHands treats caveman’s generated text as authoritative, it can commit or execute incorrect instructions without verification. Because OpenHands has downstream action authority by default, the blast radius can be irreversible, so high is appropriate.
conditions: IF OpenHands consumes caveman output as task instructions or code
IF no verification step checks caveman-generated facts before execution or commit
mitigations: Require a human approval gate before execution
Compare caveman output against source files before acting
Limit OpenHands to dry-run mode for generated plans
Separate drafting from execution roles
requires-engineering: add automated validation of generated actions

E_compliance.rationale: caveman explicitly touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while OpenHands handles files in a runtime sandbox and stores model-provider API keys. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into those files, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated-data class or jurisdiction mismatch. That keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in caveman session logs or project notes
IF OpenHands runtime retention differs from the source system’s retention policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared notes
Document retention for both tools before use
Purge runtime files after each session
Store secrets outside agent-managed files
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
